app_info.subtitle: Host and manage your websites
app_info.description:
Simple Host hosts websites you or your AI have made. Your AI puts the files online through the connector, at an address you can share, and Simple Host keeps them there. Publish a page you have made, update an existing site, or ask to see its saved entries.

Each site can save key-value data (KV), SQLite tables, and files. Access presets control who can read, add, edit, and delete data. New resources are private by default. Use an inbox for submissions only the owner reads, records for each signed-in visitor's entries with owner access, or public data for content everyone may read. Visitors sign in with Google or an emailed code; no password or sign-up form.

Update site files, preview a saved version, or restore an earlier version. The four latest site versions are kept by default, and deleted sites can be restored for 7 days. Current storage stays until you delete it or its site; it does not have automatic 30-day change history.

Connect your own domain with HTTPS or choose a short name.simple-host.app address. Manage who can open a site, read visitor counts and top pages, and download a copy of your site.

Connect your Simple Host account through the app's sign-in flow. You can revoke the connection from the Simple Host dashboard. Simple Host is open source, made and run by Vineet Sriram.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only returns the signed-in account's email, handle and public page address; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own account on Simple Host; it does not reach the public internet or any third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists the person's sites with their address and live version; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own account data; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only returns one site's details and file list; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only returns the contents of one file from the person's site; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists a site's kept versions and which one is live; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reports whether a site's domain is connected; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site settings; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only returns visit totals, the most viewed pages and the domains visitors came from for one of the person's sites; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site statistics; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Each call creates a new 10-minute download link on the server, so it is not a pure read.
justifications.open_world_justification: The link is handed to the person in the chat; nothing is published or sent anywhere, and it works only for that one site.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is changed, overwritten or deleted; it only packages a copy of the person's own site.

justifications.read_only_justification: It publishes a new website, so it creates data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The new site is published to the public internet at a public address anyone can open.
justifications.destructive_justification: It only creates: it fails if a site with that name already exists, so nothing is overwritten or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a credential that can publish a site from a shell.
justifications.open_world_justification: A successful upload publishes the site at its public address.
justifications.destructive_justification: The upload can replace the live files of an existing site. Its previous version is kept for rollback.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a one-time upload page that publishes a site from the person's WordPress export.
justifications.open_world_justification: The import publishes the converted site at its public address.
justifications.destructive_justification: The import can replace the live files of an existing site. Its previous version is kept for rollback.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reads the progress and result of the person's own import.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the person's own import on Simple Host.
justifications.destructive_justification: It changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It replaces a site's live files, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The change is published to a public website anyone can open.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites the site's live files. The previous version is kept and can be restored with rollback_site, but the overwrite itself is marked destructive.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes which version of a site is live, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It changes what the public sees on a public website.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: the replaced version is kept and can be made live again the same way.

justifications.read_only_justification: Each call mints a new short-lived preview link on the server, so it is not a pure read.
justifications.open_world_justification: The link is for the signed-in person only and publishes nothing; the version is shown only to whoever holds the one-hour link.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is changed or deleted; the live site stays as it is.

justifications.read_only_justification: It deletes a site, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It acts only inside the person's own account and publishes nothing to the internet or any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: It takes the site offline with all its versions and its saved data. It stays restorable for 7 days (restore_site), then it is removed for good. It requires the site name to be repeated as confirmation.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists the person's own recently deleted sites; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the person's own account.
justifications.destructive_justification: It changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It brings a deleted site back, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The restored site is live again on the public internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: the site comes back exactly as it was.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes a site's name and address, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The site is served at a new public address on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted; renaming it back restores the old address.

justifications.read_only_justification: It replaces the plain-text bio on the person's public page, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The bio is shown on the person's public page on the internet, so it changes what the public sees.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites the previous bio, and the old text is not kept anywhere, so the change cannot be undone by the server. The description tells the model to ask the person before replacing or clearing a bio they wrote.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes the public showcase pin and manual order of an owned site.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes what the public showcase displays.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reversible setting; no site or data is deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes the personal home-page choice.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes the page served at the public personal address.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reversible setting; no site or data is deleted.

justifications.readOnlyHint: Changes the site retention setting and prunes history.
justifications.destructiveHint: Removes older version copies for good; the live version always stays. Only operator-allowed accounts can change the count.
justifications.openWorldHint: Changes stored history only; it does not publish anything.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes whether a site is listed, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It adds a site to, or removes it from, the person's public listing page on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted and the change is fully reversible.

justifications.read_only_justification: It takes a site offline or back online, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It changes what the public sees at the site's address on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: files, versions and saved data are kept, and calling it with the other value puts the site back exactly as it was.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reports whether one of the person's own sites has a passcode and, to its owner, what the passcode is and when it was set; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site settings on Simple Host; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It puts a passcode on the person's own site, or changes the one it has, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: Every public address of the site then shows "This site is protected" until a visitor enters the passcode, so it changes what the public sees on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changing a passcode replaces the earlier one, which is not kept, and every visitor who unlocked the site with it loses access and must be given the new one; that cannot be undone. Files, versions and saved data are not touched. The description tells the model to ask the person first and to use the passcode they chose.

justifications.read_only_justification: It takes the passcode off the person's own site, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The site opens to everyone with its address again, so it changes what the public sees on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: files, versions and saved data are kept, and a passcode can be put back with set_site_passcode. The description tells the model to ask the person first.

justifications.read_only_justification: It ends every visitor's unlock of the person's own passcode-protected site, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: Every visitor sees "This site is protected" again on the public site until they re-enter the passcode, so it changes what the public sees.
justifications.destructive_justification: Every visitor's unlock ends at once and cannot be restored: each visitor must be given the passcode again to get back in. The passcode itself does not change.

justifications.read_only_justification: It marks a site Keep or clears the mark, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The mark decides whether a public site on the internet can be flagged by the idle-site cleanup.
justifications.destructive_justification: It changes a flag only; nothing is deleted or published, and the other value undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only returns ready-made page code and the resource setup for a storage job (topics records, form, gallery); it reads no site and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It returns static reference text; nothing is published, read from, or sent to any external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists the resources (KV, SQLite, files) the owner has declared on one of their sites, with each one's read and write policy; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site configuration; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reports one site's KV/SQLite/file byte usage, allowance and breakdown by kind; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates or changes a KV, SQLite or file resource's whole-resource read and write policy on the person's site, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: A resource with read:anyone or write:anyone is reachable by any visitor on the public internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changing an existing resource's policy can expose data that was private, or permit writes that were refused before; the kind cannot later change. For each person's own records (orders, RSVPs, bookings), use read:own, write:signed-in, write_mode:add, then storage_sql_schema for its tables.

justifications.read_only_justification: It permanently deletes a storage resource and all the rows, keys or files it holds, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It acts only on the owner's own site storage; nothing is published or sent to any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is irreversible: the resource and everything in it are gone for good. Ask the owner to confirm the exact resource name first.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists the keys stored in one KV resource (optionally by prefix); it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site storage; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reads one JSON value from a KV resource; it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site storage; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates or replaces one JSON value in a KV resource, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: A resource with a public read policy exposes the value to any visitor on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites any existing value at that key with no history kept; ask the owner before overwriting.

justifications.read_only_justification: It removes one JSON value from a KV resource, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It acts only on the owner's own site storage; nothing is published or sent to any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is irreversible: the value is gone for good. Ask the owner to confirm before deleting.

justifications.read_only_justification: The server's SQLite authorizer enforces that this call only reads rows; it cannot change anything even if asked to.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site storage, including every visitor's rows as the owner; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It runs an INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statement against a SQLite resource's rows, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: A resource with a public or signed-in read policy shows the changed rows to visitors.
justifications.destructive_justification: It can overwrite or permanently remove rows with no built-in undo; ask the owner before changing or deleting rows.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates or changes the tables of a SQLite resource (owner only), so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It acts only on the owner's own site storage; nothing is published or sent to any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: A schema change can remove or reshape existing data (for example dropping a column); ask the owner first.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only lists the file paths stored in a files resource (optionally by prefix); it changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own site storage; nothing is published or sent anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is created, changed or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: It uploads or replaces one file's bytes in a files resource, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: A resource with a public read policy serves the file to any visitor on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites any existing file at that path with no history kept; ask the owner before overwriting.

justifications.read_only_justification: It removes one file from a files resource, so it changes data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It acts only on the owner's own site storage; nothing is published or sent to any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is irreversible: the file is gone for good. Ask the owner to confirm before deleting.

justifications.read_only_justification: Each call mints a new short-lived, scoped download link for one file's bytes on the server, so it is not a pure read.
justifications.open_world_justification: The link is for the signed-in owner only and is given to them in the chat; nothing is published or sent anywhere else.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is changed or deleted; it only mints a link to existing bytes.

justifications.read_only_justification: It gives a site a new address, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The site is served at a new public address: a free name.simple-host.app address or a domain the person owns on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted; the site's existing address and content are unchanged.

justifications.read_only_justification: It disconnects a site's domain, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The public site moves to a different public address, and the disconnected domain becomes free for someone else on the internet to connect.
justifications.destructive_justification: Links to a disconnected custom domain stop working; the person must confirm by typing the domain, and the tool asks for explicit confirmation first.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes who can open a site, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It changes what the public sees at the site's address on the internet: everyone but named viewers gets a sign-in page.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: files, versions, saved data and the list of named viewers are kept, and the other value puts the site back as it was.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reads who can open one of the person's sites.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own account only.
justifications.destructive_justification: It changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It adds named viewers to a site and opens it only to them, so it modifies data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It changes what the public sees at the site's address on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted, and revoke_site_viewer or set_site_access undoes it.

justifications.read_only_justification: It removes one person from the site's named viewers, which changes who can open the site: from their next page view that person can no longer open it and sees "This site is private" instead. That is a user-visible side effect for the removed person and for the owner, who sees them gone from list_site_viewers.
justifications.open_world_justification: It changes who can open the site's public address on the internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: The person loses access to the site immediately; access comes back only if the owner grants it again with grant_site_viewer.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reads which email signed in for record ids on the person's own site.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads the person's own account only.
justifications.destructive_justification: It changes nothing.

test_cases.description: Publish supplied replacement page files to the seeded garden party site.
test_cases.user_prompt: Publish these supplied page files to my existing garden-party-rsvp site. Keep its saved RSVPs.
test_cases.expected_output: Publishes the supplied index.html and style.css to garden-party-rsvp and returns its address. Existing RSVP storage is unchanged. No unsolicited photo, notification, or identity calls.

test_cases.description: Update the seeded feedback survey and undo the requested change.
test_cases.user_prompt: On feedback-survey, change the heading to "Tell us how we did". Then, in the same chat: Undo that change.
test_cases.expected_output: The survey shows the requested heading. After confirmation of the rollback, the previous version restores the original heading. No account or visitor emails are returned.

test_cases.description: Read only the requested order details from the seeded pickle shop.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show the orders saved by pickle-shop, including items, totals, and status.
test_cases.expected_output: Queries only items, total_cents, and status in the orders resource and returns the four seeded orders. No customer names, contacts, emails, or unrelated records are returned, and nothing is changed.

test_cases.user_prompt: How many RSVPs do I have on garden-party-rsvp?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns COUNT(*) from the rsvps table in the rsvps resource, matching the current fixture count. Returns no emails, names, or visitor references. Does not call who_am_i or storage_visitor_emails.

test_cases.description: Identify only the signed-in test visitor who submitted one RSVP.
test_cases.user_prompt: Who submitted the RSVP named "Reviewer identity check" on garden-party-rsvp? Give me only that person's sign-in email.
test_cases.expected_output: Queries only visitor_id for the single RSVP named Reviewer identity check, then passes that per-site opaque reference to storage_visitor_emails for garden-party-rsvp. Returns only that person's email, with no other visitor emails or internal account IDs. Requires the signed-in RSVP fixture described in this kit.

negative_test_cases.description: Brainstorming does not authorize hosting or account access.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Help me brainstorm names for my new hair salon.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Answers in chat with name ideas. Does not call any Simple Host tool or publish anything.

negative_test_cases.description: An uploaded server application is outside the hosting service.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy my Node.js API with a Postgres database to production.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains that Simple Host serves static files and its built-in storage; it does not run your own server code. No deployment occurs. Offers to discuss a static frontend if useful.

negative_test_cases.description: Summarizing an unrelated external website is outside the connector.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarize what is on https://example.com for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explains that Simple Host does not retrieve arbitrary external pages. Makes no Simple Host call and does not direct another connector to run.
